q: How does ripgrep search inside gzip, bzip2 or zstd archives?
why: DecompressionMatcherBuilder maps extension globs (*.gz, *.zst, ...) to external filter binaries spawned via CommandReader, whose stdout is then searched.

q: How does ripgrep detect binary data while streaming a file and decide whether to quit or convert it?
why: LineBuffer::fill scans each freshly read chunk for the configured binary byte (NUL) and implements BinaryDetection::{Quit,Convert} with binary_byte_offset tracking.

q: Where is parallel directory traversal with worker threads implemented?
why: WalkParallel drives crossbeam_deque Worker/Stealer threads over walkdir, each carrying a per-directory Ignore stack.

q: How are capture group references like $1 or $name expanded when replacing matched text?
why: interpolate() scans the replacement for $N/${name} references via find_cap_ref and appends the resolved capture text to the destination buffer.

q: How does ripgrep search files encoded in UTF-16 or carrying a byte-order mark?
why: The searcher Config's encoding/bom_sniffing options drive encoding_rs_io::DecodeReaderBytesBuilder to transcode input to UTF-8 before matching.

q: Where is the human-readable match output with colors, headings and context lines produced?
why: The Standard printer's Sink impl writes colored path/line-number headers plus match and before/after context blocks using termcolor.

q: What rejects a regex that is capable of matching the line terminator byte?
why: ban::check recursively walks the pattern HIR and returns ErrorKind::Banned when any sub-expression must match the forbidden byte (called from config.rs).

q: How does ripgrep decide which directory entries are actually worth searching?
why: HaystackBuilder filters walk results by file type / stdin / explicit-argument status and yields a Haystack only for searchable entries.

q: Where is the code that generates the Deserialize implementation for user structs and enums?
why: expand_derive_deserialize builds the impl TokenStream from the Container AST, dispatching bodies to the struct_/tuple/enum_* submodules.

q: How are #[serde(...)] attributes on containers, variants and fields parsed during macro expansion?
why: Module docs state this module parses #[serde(...)] attributes via Container/Variant/Field::from_ast, accumulating every malformed attribute error in Ctxt.

q: What lets serde efficiently discard data it does not care about during deserialization?
why: IgnoredAny implements Deserialize/Visitor for any input while storing nothing, used to skip unknown fields and unwanted sequence elements.

q: How does serde buffer arbitrary input values to support untagged enum deserialization?
why: The hidden Content enum buffers an entire Deserializer's data so generated code can retry variants for untagged and internally tagged enums.

q: How does ripgrep test thousands of `*.rs`-style wildcard patterns against a file path without running a full regex for each one?
why: MatchStrategy::new classifies each parsed pattern as Literal/BasenameLiteral/Extension/Prefix/Suffix/RequiredExtension so matching can use hash-table lookups, falling back to Regex only when necessary; Glob also stores the tokenized pattern and its compiled regex equivalent.

q: How does ripgrep avoid running the full automaton on every line by first hunting for short mandatory byte sequences?
why: InnerLiterals::new extracts an inner literal Seq from the pattern HIR (skipping when no line terminator is set or the regex is already accelerated) so a fast vectorized substring scan finds candidate lines and the slow engine only runs on those lines.

q: How can a type be written straight into a Formatter through its Display implementation, without serde building an intermediate String?
why: Serializer is implemented for &mut fmt::Formatter: primitives and unit variants forward to Display::fmt via the fmt_primitives! macro while compound types return Impossible errors, backing Serializer::collect_str.

q: How does serde know how to deserialize tuples, Option, primitives and standard collections when no derive macro is involved?
why: This module hand-writes Deserialize impls for (), bool, numbers, Option, tuples (via TupleVisitor) and maps/sequences, each pairing a small Visitor with the matching deserialize_* call on the Deserializer.

q: Where is the RegexMatcherBuilder for the PCRE2 engine, and how does it implement smart case and --fixed-strings?
why: pcre2's RegexMatcherBuilder::build_many joins patterns, escapes them when fixed_strings is set, enables caseless matching when case_smart and no uppercase literal is present, wraps whole_line/word variants, and records capture names in RegexMatcher.

q: Where is OverrideBuilder and how do -g/--glob whitelist patterns get inverted into ignore semantics?
why: Override wraps a Gitignore built by OverrideBuilder; because whitelist globs mean 'only search these', matched() reports non-matches as ignored (UnmatchedIgnore) and swaps num_ignores/num_whitelists.

q: Where is FlatMapDeserializer and how does it make #[serde(flatten)] work at runtime?
why: FlatMapDeserializer replays buffered key-value pairs into flattened fields (entries nulled out as claimed), while missing_field and the TaggedContentVisitor/UntaggedUnitVisitor helpers here support derive-generated code.

q: Where does serde define `impl Serialize for Option<T>` and the Serialize impls for primitives, str and collections?
why: The primitive_impl! macro forwards each number/bool/char to the matching Serializer::serialize_* method, and hand-written impls for Option, str, String, slices and Vec delegate to serialize_str/serialize_seq and friends.
